Bishop Hill fully demolished, residents did not protest

Su said he received the demolition notice at the end of July and immediately contacted the Sham Shui Po District Councillor to request the preservation of the fitness equipment on Wozi Mountain, but was told "no equipment will be preserved". Su noted that in the past, residents had organised petitions to protest against demolitions, but this time the notification period was too short to organise opposition. As a result, a morning exercise spot used by residents for over 20 years will soon be gone.

Three days ago (the 10th), the Home Affairs Department announced the Wozi Mountain optimisation plan, stating that the government will clear illegal and unsafe structures, facilities, or杂物 on the mountain in phases, noting that these objects have long illegally occupied government land.

Yesterday (the 12th), at around 6:30am, staff from the Lands Department and uniformed police arrived, cordoning off the area from the base to the summit of the Tongyin Street hillside rest area. Movers immediately began removing fitness equipment, bicycles, ping-pong tables, and other items. Police deployed冲锋车 (Unimog) and 豬籠車 (prisoner transport vehicles) as security. Su said this is merely a place for residents to exercise, and he does not understand the purpose of the police deployment. "The officers just stood there, watching us the whole time. What have we done? Are we rioters? Have we broken the law?"

"Morning Exercise Haven" becomes LCSD facility

Su noted that residents collectively raised HK$400,000 to build the Bishop Hill "Morning Exercise Haven", including ping-pong tables, fitness equipment, and unofficial hiking trails built decades ago. On the day of the demolition, many residents were still doing morning exercises and using the fitness equipment. Several residents expressed deep sorrow at the loss of their long-time exercise spot. Some residents kept asking Mr Su what to do, but Mr Su himself did not know what to say.

He said he spent several days moving the fitness equipment away, hoping to preserve what he had built with his own hands. Currently, he has removed all muscle massage rollers, while some residents intend to move parts of the statues to Lantau Island.

According to the Home Affairs Department's Wozi Mountain optimisation plan, the "Morning Exercise Haven" will become an LCSD facility. The DIY fitness equipment on the mountain will be replaced with standard LCSD recreational equipment; as for the statues, religious leaders will visit to handle them properly.

Miraculous survival leads to building Bishop Hill "Morning Exercise Haven"

75-year-old Su Chi-keung is a SARS survivor. Due to medication side effects, he suffered后遗症 such as muscle pain, weakness, and fatigue. After three years of physiotherapy, his condition did not improve. In 2008, Su was invited by a neighbour to Bishop Hill. After morning exercise, he noticed his spirits improved, which he attributed to the fresh mountain air. He thus began exercising at Bishop Hill every morning at 6am. After persisting for a month, he recovered his health and stamina, and decided to stop physiotherapy.

In 2009, Mr Su travelled to South Korea and was inspired by the local fitness facilities. After returning to Hong Kong, he referenced the designs and "DIY-built" a stationary bike and a cable machine at his own hardware factory. He single-handedly transported the fitness equipment in pieces up Bishop Hill, describing the construction as simple but the transportation as extremely arduous. Over four years, he built more than 20 fitness facilities on Bishop Hill, including swings, balance bars, rollers, etc., and placed them on the open ground above the current Sham Shui Po service reservoir. At the time, some elderly residents opposed him, but after other residents used the facilities and found relief from physical ailments, they became very popular.

Bishop Hill first exposed to public, residents protest against demolition

Su noted that in 2014, more than 200 young people held a rave party on Bishop Hill, causing noise disturbance. When police arrived, they discovered for the first time a large number of private fitness facilities. Subsequently, the Water Supplies Department increased patrols on Bishop Hill and repeatedly drove away residents exercising there, planning to demolish the facilities. At that time, Mr Su organised several protest activities and went in person to the Sham Shui Po District Council Secretariat to fight for the preservation of the fitness area.

Unexpected viral moment makes Bishop Hill reservoir a Grade 1 historic building

In 2017, the Water Supplies Department planned to clear unauthorised structures on Bishop Hill and return the land to the Lands Department. Combined with the fact that two large trees on the reservoir roof had roots extending into the structure, posing a collapse risk, the department prepared to remove the trees and backfill the reservoir. In 2020, the Water Supplies Department promised Mr Su that his fitness facilities could be placed on the backfilled land, and Su agreed to the work.

However, on Christmas Eve, Mr Su and a volunteer sneaked into the reservoir to check if anything had been left behind, took photos, and posted them on social media. This attracted large crowds to visit the reservoir, sparking public attention. Su noted that the public protested the demolition because of the reservoir's historical value. One resident who frequently visited Bishop Hill, Ms Fong, even stood in front of an excavator to stop the demolition work.

In 2021, the reservoir was graded as a Grade 1 historic building by the Antiquities Advisory Board. The reservoir was preserved and opened to the public, and Mr Su moved the fitness facilities to the base of the mountain.

Mao Zedong statue incident may have triggered the demolition

In June 2022, the Sham Shui Po District Management Committee intended to remove the shrines and fitness facilities. Mr Su launched a petition to demand their preservation, stating that 3,399 Sham Shui Po District residents signed, and he delivered a letter to the Home Affairs Department, promising not to expand the facilities further.

Su noted that after this, Bishop Hill remained peaceful, and the government did not indicate that a clearance was necessary. However, in early 2026, resident Ms Fong set up a Mao Zedong statue and Mao Zedong Cultural Hall on Bishop Hill. Although they were later removed, Su believes that the Mao Zedong incident revived the government's attention to Bishop Hill. Coupled with some residents making loud noises on the mountain, disturbing nearby residents, the government decided to fully demolish Bishop Hill.

In early 2026, resident Ms Fong set up a Mao Zedong statue and Mao Zedong Cultural Hall on Bishop Hill, reigniting controversy over the use of the hill. (File photo)

"Without Bishop Hill, I would have lived 20 years less"

Watching workers dismantle the fitness equipment he built one by one, Su did not show grief. He plans to bring the dismantled fitness equipment back to his ancestral home and continues to tell the media about Bishop Hill's history. In fact, he is fully aware that Bishop Hill is highly controversial, with the "Morning Exercise Haven" having been unauthorised for years, but he believes the place has long benefited many residents. He hopes that by telling Bishop Hill's story, he will gain the government's recognition. Although the site ultimately was not preserved, he still wishes to pass on the story to repay Bishop Hill for what it has given him.

He bid farewell to Bishop Hill: "I am grateful it gave me a new life. Without it, I would be 20 years shorter. I should have died. If not for Bishop Hill, I would have died... Besides, I am an injured SARS survivor. Do you think I could still be alive today?"
